_meta.note: RE-REVIEW supplement to S248. The pilvar222 X thread ingested in S248 was promoting Aikido's full blog 'Benchmarking 13 AI Models on Known CVE Detection' (aikido.dev). That ORIGINAL run used 26 CVEs / 13 models; S248 captured only the later GLM-5.3-era UPDATE run (harder/expanded set: pass@3 % where gpt-5.6-terra=68, GLM-5.3=75 leads; consistency /32). Because the two runs use different CVE-set sizes, the same model legitimately has two different values (e.g. gpt-5.6-terra 23/26=88.5% original vs 68% update) — they MUST live in separate benchmark ids or they would collide under INSERT OR REPLACE. This file adds the ORIGINAL 26-CVE run as its own id 'aikido_cve_rediscovery_26cve'. Values are pass@3 (union of 3 pooled runs) recall, taken ONLY from precise prose figures (charts are images, not extractable). Percentages = count/26. STRICT ATTRIBUTION: skipped 'the Claude Opus models (15 to 18)' — a range across unnamed variants, not a per-model value. GPT-5.6 headline 23/26 assigned to sol (flagship = the canonical 'GPT-5.6'); terra 23 is explicit ('the same 23'). Kimi K3 was added post-publication per the article.

benchmarks.name: Aikido CVE-Rediscovery pass@3 (26-CVE original run)
benchmarks._note: Recall = fraction of 26 known CVEs rediscovered by the union of 3 pooled runs (pass@3). ORIGINAL Aikido blog run (13 models). Distinct from aikido_cve_rediscovery_pass3, which is the later GLM-5.3-era update on an expanded/harder set.

scores._note: 23/26 = 88.5%. 'GPT-5.6 gets the highest recall score, topping out at 23/26 ... 88.5% of CVEs.' Assigned to Sol as the flagship 'GPT-5.6'.
23/26 = 88.5%. 'gpt-5.6-terra ... 2.2x the cost for the same 23.' (Same model scores 68% on the later 32-CVE update run in aikido_cve_rediscovery_pass3 — different CVE set.)
23/26 = 88.5%. 'able to rediscover 23/26 CVEs on our harness ... 4x cheaper than GPT-5.6-Sol.' Strongest OSS model; added post-publication.
18/26 = 69.2%. 'Three runs of gpt-5.4-nano cost about $170 and reach 18/26.'
16/26 = 61.5%. 'GLM-5.2 already rediscovers 59% of the set (16/26)' — count 16/26 is the explicit figure; article's 59% phrasing is a loose rounding.
